original_question: Determine whether higher-dimensional black holes are stable under gravitational perturbations, including the kinds of instabilities that do not occur in four-dimensional general relativity.
target_in_paper: Section 4.2 ("Higher dimensions"), Problem P10: "Determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies higher-dimensional black holes as the target, treats stability as the core issue, and reflects the nearby §4.2 discussion that frames the problem through gravitational perturbations and specifically higher-dimensional instability phenomena not present in 4D. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
missing_details: The official formulation is not a yes/no question ('whether higher-dimensional black holes are stable') but an open-ended classification/problem of analysis: 'determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
The paper's setting is classical general relativity in spacetime dimension greater than four; a stand-alone version should say this explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

The formal problem statement P10 does not itself specify 'under gravitational perturbations'; that perturbative lens comes from the immediately following explanatory discussion, so it should be presented as paper-guided sharpening rather than verbatim official wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

The nearby context motivates P10 by emphasizing that higher-dimensional gravity has a richer black-hole solution space than 4D, including multiple asymptotically flat higher-dimensional vacuum solutions; your draft does not state that scope/motivation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

If the clause about instabilities absent in 4D is kept, the paper's concrete examples should be named: Gregory-Laflamme instability (first for black strings and black p-branes), instabilities of black rings, and the ultraspinning instability of rapidly rotating Myers-Perry black holes in dimensions greater than 6. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

The discussion links these instabilities to possible failure of weak cosmic censorship in higher dimensions, but that is motivation/context rather than part of the formal wording of P10. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

No algebraic ambient data are relevant here: the paper gives no ring/field, operator-domain, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'for all sufficiently large m' conditions, because P10 is posed as a geometric-relativistic open problem rather than a formally parameterized theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
refined_question: In classical general relativity with spacetime dimension D > 4, determine the stability of higher-dimensional black holes under gravitational perturbations, i.e. identify which higher-dimensional black-hole families are stable and which exhibit genuinely higher-dimensional instabilities absent in four-dimensional GR, such as Gregory-Laflamme-type and ultraspinning instabilities. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
justification: This draft is targeting the survey's official open problem P10 in §4.2, not a conjecture/proposition/theorem elsewhere: the paper explicitly states 'Determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes.' The added language about gravitational perturbations and 4D-exotic instability channels comes from the immediately adjacent explanatory paragraphs, which mention gravitational-perturbation instability, Gregory-Laflamme instability, black-ring instabilities, and ultraspinning instability of Myers-Perry black holes. The paper does not provide a formally equivalent reformulation of P10 nearby, so no alternate formulation should be invented. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
